To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of counseling psychologists are familiar with and use qualitative research, and (2) counseling psychologists are concerned about the trustworthiness of qualitative research and the criteria for assessing trustworthiness.

the quality of qualitative counseling psychology research is best assessed in terms of the paradigmatic and epistemological underpinnings and assumptions of the research, the standards of trustworthiness, and the discipline in which it is conducted.
(a) the majority of counseling psychology graduate students are interested in qualitative research and (b) the majority of students are interested in publishing qualitative research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the experiences of women and men in their everyday lives, particularly as they are affected by the social, economic, and political structures in which they live.
the development and testing of theory, the description and interpretation of phenomena, or the development of a new perspective or paradigm, or a combination of all three.
how individuals make meaning of their experiences and how these meanings influence their lives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the researcher’s perspective, the paradigmatic assumptions of the research, and the standards of quality of the discipline in which the study is situated are all critical to the quality of a study.
the quality of qualitative inquiry is best assessed by the paradigmatic underpinning of the research and by the standards of the field or discipline.
the researcher has been as transparent as possible in the process of conducting the research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the research is of high quality.

the quality and trustworthiness of qualitative inquiry in counseling psychology are enhanced by the use of appropriate methods, by the use of multiple sources of evidence and multiple investigators, by the use and reporting of multiple perspectives on the phenomena being studied, and by the inclusion of the voices of participants in the research.
we believe that the purpose of qualitative research is not to prove anything but to discover, to explore, and to understand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
qualitative researchers can and should take steps to enhance the quality of their research.
we can all benefit from a better understanding of the ways in which our own values and beliefs shape how we do research and how we interpret the research we do.
qualitative research is an important part of the counseling psychology research agenda and can contribute to the knowledge base of counseling psychology.
